newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria protesters keep up pressure on government.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria protesters keep up pressure on government.

text.p: Bulgarian protesters kept up strikes and blockades around the country on Friday, piling pressure on their Socialist rulers to agree to an election.
Demonstrators at Doupnitsa, south of Sofia, blockaded the main road south to the Greek border for a third day. Working in shifts, they stayed on the barricades all night, burning tyres to keep warm.
Protesters blocked the main road south on the outskirts of the capital.
The opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) in the second city of Plovdiv said protesters planned to use buses to block the highway from Sofia to Turkey.
One-hour stoppages were reported at schools and factories around the country.
Parliament debated a stopgap budget bill drawn up by the outgoing cabinet, which will permit a doubling of state salaries to take account of soaring inflation.
The 1997 budget has been delayed by political confusion since outgoing prime minister Zhan Videnov resigned on December 21.
The national currency, in freefall since the beginning of the year, was quoted at 1,730-1,900 in the interbank market on Friday compared to 1,530-1,590 at Thursday's close.
President Petar Stoyanov headed back from a visit to Brussels, where the European Union told him not to expect any more financial support until Bulgaria restored political stability.

"The European Commission stated that, as soon as the political situation in Bulgaria allows it, it would consider taking the necessary initiatives to mobilise support for Bulgaria from the international financial institutions and the world community," the Commission said in a statement.
Before leaving Stoyanov gave the Socialists a mandate to form a government, which must then be approved by parliament.

Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev, who is struggling to form a cabinet in the face of widespread popular opposition, said he would serve only three to five months and then hold elections, but that compromise offer failed to placate the opposition, which wants elections now.
Police set up barricades near the UDF headquarters in anticipation of a possible demonstration by young Socialist supporters on Friday.

The Sofia circus was putting on a special performance for students, whose colourful, inventive daily protests rely on humour rather than confrontation. The students then plan their daily march, and to join the main opposition rally at the Alexander Nevsky cathedral.

Socialist party leader Georgi Parvanov on Thursday wrote to each party in parliament inviting them for more talks. The Socialists have said they would like to form a coalition, but other parties have declined.
Under the constitution, Dobrev has until Tuesday to form a cabinet. Parvanov told reporters he was confident the cabinet would win enough votes in a secret ballot to be approved.
